brief:
Israel's political opposition takes a harder line on Iran than Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, according to Al Jazeera English. While the international community often portrays Netanyahu as the chief architect of Israel's Iran policy, domestic rivals argue he has not pursued a sufficiently aggressive approach against Tehran.

The gap reflects deepening divisions within Israeli politics over how forcefully to confront Iranian nuclear ambitions and regional activities. Opposition figures claim Netanyahu's strategy lacks the intensity needed to counter what they characterize as an existential threat.
dek: In rest of the world, the Israeli PM is often blamed for the Iran war. His opponents say he hasn't been tough enough.
title: Israeli opposition parties outflank Netanyahu on Iran hawk stance
